title: Upsell starter kit & technical eval checklist — Dedicated / Private / SLA
summary: Working draft: compact QBR + renewal tracker + technical evaluation checklist intended for early-stage expansion conversations (Dedicated capacity, Private deployments, premium SLAs). Focus: rapid qualification, risk mitigation, and play-by-play outreach templates.
body:
Purpose
- One-page pack for CS+SEs to run an expansion conversation during QBRs or renewal windows.
- Emphasis on technical feasibility, cost delta, SLO uplift, and simple decision rubric so execs can sign off quickly.

Audience
- Primary: Customer Success Managers, Solutions Engineers, Account Execs.
- Secondary: Product Ops, Sales Engineering, Legal for T&Cs.

When to use
- QBR where customer shows >50% of current capacity utilization or growth signals (spike in request rate, token volumes).
- Renewal window within 90–180 days of contract end.
- Post-incident conversations where SLA guarantees are requested.

QBR template (1–2 slides / 1–page doc)
- Executive summary (1–2 lines): recommended path (Dedicated / Private / SLA add-on), top reason (cost predictability, compliance, latency).
- Key signals: 30d p95 latency, 30d token spend, error rate trends, paging incidents, data residency needs.
- Usage & economics: current spend (monthly), projected delta for Dedicated reserve or Private infra, estimated savings window (months to payback).
- Technical readiness: network pre-reqs, data flows, security approvals needed.
- Recommendation & ask: one clear CTA (e.g., "Approve pilot: 2-week Private proof-of-concept" or "Approve Dedicated 3-month reserved capacity commit").
- Next steps & owners (who will perform sizing, legal, deployment, SRE ramp).

Renewal tracker (lightweight, copyable)
- Account: <ACME Corp>
- Renewal date: 2026-05-15
- Current tier: Hosted API (pay-as-you-go)
- Signals: 40% QoS incidents (last 6 months), 2x growth M/M, Token run-rate $18k/mo
- Recommended path: Dedicated 4-GPU pool + premium SLA (99.95%)
- Estimated economics: +$12k/mo committed vs current; estimated 25% per-token cost reduction at scale; 3-month payback on migration engineering time
- Risks: network peering, cert rotation KMS, PCI scope increase
- Owner: Priya Nair (CS), SE: Ethan Park, Legal intake: Leah Gomez

Outreach / cadence (6–8 week play)
- Week 0: QBR — present recommendation + exec ask (15 min)
- Week 1: Technical deep-dive (SE + infra call) — checklist review, sizing 
- Week 2: Procurement touchpoint (pricing, SOW template)
- Week 3–4: Pilot (if Private): run smoke tests, confirm observability hooks
- Week 5: Post-pilot review + SLA contract redlines
- Week 6+: Go/no-go & kickoff migration/rollout

Email templates (short, copyable)
- Exec ask (subject): "Proposal: Dedicated capacity to stabilize latency & reduce unit cost"
Body (short): "Hi <Name>, during our QBR we observed sustained growth in token usage and several latency spikes affecting your UX. We recommend a Dedicated pool (4 x A100-equivalent) plus 99.95% SLA to stabilize SLA and reduce unit costs. Can we get 15 minutes to review the delta and expected ROI?"

- Technical invite (subject): "Technical deep-dive: Dedicated/Private feasibility for <ACME>"
Body: "SEs + infra — can we align on network/topology and test plan? Key items: egress rules, peering, KMS access, model pinning, traffic split strategy. I propose Tuesday 10am PT."

Technical evaluation checklist (for SE to run during Week 1 call)
- Account profile
  - Data classification: PII / highly regulated / none
  - Required regions: US, EU, APAC?
- Networking
  - VPC peering or PrivateLink required? (yes/no)
  - CIDR & firewall rules documented? (ask for network diagram)
  - Egress bandwidth profile / burst patterns (sample logs)
- Security & compliance
  - KMS / HSM: customer-managed keys required? (KMS SKU)
  - Audit log retention requirements (90/180/365 days)
  - SOC2 / ISO evidence needed?
  - Data residency / on-prem requirement?
- Performance targets
  - Target p50/p95/p99 latencies for primary flows
  - Throughput requirements (reqs/sec, tokens/sec) and concurrency patterns
  - KV cache hit-rate expectations (are they using prefix reuse?)
- Model / Serving concerns
  - Which models are needed (open/Redwood-verified/custom)?
  - Want model pinning for deterministic behavior?
  - Quantization / accuracy tolerance? (0.5%/1% acceptable delta?)
- Observability & SLOs
  - Trace/span hooks required? (open telemetry, headers)
  - Token-level cost reporting needed?
  - Alert thresholds and on-call escalation contacts
- Deployment constraints
  - Maintenance windows, blackout dates
  - SLA escalation path acceptance (ops contacts)
- Pilot test plan (if Private)
  - Smoke tests (latency, correctness, failure injection)
  - Load test targets (2x current peak for 30 minutes)
  - Regression prompt set (baseline prompts + golden outputs)
  - Rollback criteria (errors >2% or latency p95 > target+2x)

Decision rubric (quick scorecard)
- Weightings (example): cost delta 30%, reliability gain 30%, compliance fit 20%, engineering effort 20%
- Scoring: 1–5 per axis (1 low, 5 high).
- Threshold: score >= 16 => pursue Dedicated/Private with SOW. 12–15 => run pilot. <12 => recommend hosted optimizations first.

Economics primer (how to estimate impact)
- Inputs: current tokens/mo, current cost/mo, estimated tokens/mo growth, Dedicated reserved unit price, expected latency-enabled revenue impact (e.g., conversion uptick).
- Quick calc: incremental_commit = reserved_monthly_rate - current_average_monthly_spend
  - expected_unit_cost_reduction = (hosted_unit_cost - dedicated_unit_cost) * tokens/mo
  - simple payback months = incremental_commit / expected_monthly_savings
- Tip: include engineering migration hours in cost (use blended hourly rate from finance template).

Playbook scenarios (short)
- Fast path (low friction): customer ok with Dedicated but not Private. Offer 3-month reserved commit with canary routing. Minimal networking changes.
- Pilot path (compliance/regulatory): Private pilot in staging VPC for 2–4 weeks; include P0 test plan and observability kick.
- SLA-only path: keep hosted footprint, add premium SLA + runbook; requires legal redlines but no infra changes. Good when cost delta unacceptable.

Risk log (common blockers)
- Network peering denied or delayed by customer netops
- KMS onboarding delays push schedule 2–4w
- Model accuracy regressions after quantization -> need regression suite
- Procurement cycle / sticker shock on committed spend

Rollback template (if upgrade causes regressions)
- Trigger: post-cutover >2% critical error increase OR key metric regressions per regression suite
- Immediate steps: divert traffic back to hosted variant, open incident with SRE, capture perf traces and golden prompt diffs
- Postmortem: 72-hour RCA, recommended rollback window, plan for retest

Notes to self / open questions
- Should we formalize a standard Reserved SKU pack (e.g., "Dedicated-4", "Dedicated-8") for faster procurement? (engineering pricing team ok with this?)
- Need legal template for SLA add-ons + incident credit calc — Leah to draft
- Consider adding a brief cost-visual (sparkline) for QBR slide deck (Finance/BI to help)

Next steps (owner-action list)
- Create pricing SOW template (Owner: Leah Gomez, due: 1 week)
- Build pilot runbook checklist in GitHub (Owner: Ethan Park, due: 2 weeks)
- Add standard Reserved SKUs to pricing sheet (Owner: Marcus Reed, due: 3 weeks)

Appendix: quick copy snippets
- Executive ask (short): "Approve pilot for Private staging (2 weeks) to validate latency and compliance requirements. SEs will own test plan and smoke tests; CS will own exec comms."
- Pilot acceptance criteria (short): "latency p95 <= target, golden prompts pass, no regression >1%"

End of draft — leave comments inline and tag owners for follow-up.

(working doc — intentionally succinct; meant to be copied into QBR slide notes and Confluence playbook afterwards)
